widget.agents_md:
# Widget Agent — Workflow

## Fixing / updating existing widgets

When the user says an existing widget has wrong data, wrong months, wrong labels, etc.:
1. **Do NOT create a new widget** — update the existing one
2. For chart widgets (bar, pie, line-chart, kpi): use the DB API to clear and re-seed data:
   ```python
   # Clear existing rows, then insert correct ones
   # GET /db/widget/{canvasId}/rows?sessionId={sessionId}
   # DELETE /db/widget/{canvasId}/rows/{id} for each row
   # POST /db/widget/{canvasId}/rows with correct data
   ```
3. For code-based widgets: use FileEdit on `{session_dir}/custom_widgets/{canvasId}.js`
4. Tell the user which canvasId was updated (visible in the widget header)

**Never deploy a second widget when the user asks to fix or update an existing one.**

## Creating widgets

Whenever the user asks to create/build/add/vibe-code a widget:
1. **Always invoke `/new-widget` skill first** — for EVERY widget request, including follow-up or similar requests
2. Follow the skill instructions precisely — never skip or shortcut the skill

**Never** call `curl`, `POST /canvas/deploy-widget`, or any HTTP endpoint to create widgets. Always use the Python script from the skill.

**Never** write custom JavaScript from scratch when a built-in template matches. Writing custom code for chart types (pie, bar, line, kpi) wastes tokens and produces worse results than the template.

## Modifying existing widgets

Read the widget code from `server_data/custom_widgets/{canvasId}.js`, edit it with FileEdit, done — no skill needed.

skills.new-widget:
# Skill: new-widget

## Step 1 — Match to a built-in template FIRST

Always prefer a built-in template over writing code from scratch.
Use the table below to match the user’s request to a template name:

{widget_template_table}

If matched — deploy with one command (no file writing):
```
$BZ_PYTHON {scripts_path}/create-widget.py --title "<name>" --template <template-name> --session-dir {session_dir} --cwd {working_dir}
```

```

### Templates with user-specified data (pie, bar, kpi, line-chart)
When the user asks for a chart with **specific data values** (e.g. "pie chart of trading stats: 54% winning, 30% losing"):
- **Still use `--template`** — do NOT write custom code
- Built-in chart templates have an **"Edit data"** button — the user can update values directly in the UI
- Tell the user: "I've deployed the pie chart — click **Edit data** to enter your trading stats values"
- Only seed data programmatically (via DB API) if the user provides exact values AND explicitly asks for them to be pre-filled

Deploying the template is ALWAYS cheaper and more reliable than writing custom chart code.

## Step 2 — Custom code only if no template matches

Write self-contained JS, then deploy:
1. FileWrite the widget JS to `{server_data_path}/custom_widgets/.pending.js`
2. `$BZ_PYTHON {scripts_path}/create-widget.py --title "<name>" --session-dir {session_dir} --cwd {working_dir} [--w 380] [--h 280]`

### Rules for custom widgets
- Root: `height:100vh; overflow:hidden; background:var(--bg-primary); color:var(--text-primary)`
- CSS vars only — no hex. Key vars: `--bg-primary --text-primary --text-secondary --border-primary --accent-blue --accent-green --accent-red --radius-md --font-body`
- Guard all db calls: `if(window.db){ ... }` — db is null in preview
- db API: `await db.ensure([{name,type}])` · `await db.query({order,dir,limit})→{rows}` · `await db.insert({...})` · `await db.update(id,{...})` · `await db.delete(id)`
- CDN libs: `const s=document.createElement('script');s.src='URL';s.onload=()=>{};document.head.appendChild(s)`

Canvas reloads automatically. Tell user: ✓ **[Name]** added to canvas.

worker.agents_md:
# Worker Agent — Workflow

## Reading documents

When the user references a file:
1. **If they ask a specific question about content** — use extract-doc first (saves 80–90% tokens):
   ```
   $BZ_PYTHON {scripts_path}/extract-doc.py --path <absolute_file_path> --query "<what to find>"
   ```
2. **If they want a full summary** — read the whole document:
   ```
   $BZ_PYTHON {scripts_path}/read-doc.py --path <absolute_file_path>
   ```
3. For Excel, pass `--sheet "Sheet Name"` to both scripts to focus on a specific sheet.
4. Quote precisely — reference page numbers or sheet names when citing content.

## Comparing documents

When asked to compare, review changes, or find differences between two files:
```
$BZ_PYTHON {scripts_path}/diff-docs.py --before <old_file> --after <new_file>
```
Never read both documents manually — always use the diff script.

## Creating Word documents

Always use the `/new-doc` skill first — it matches a template so you write only the variable content, not the entire structure.

**Never** write a full document from scratch when a template matches. Templates: report, meeting-minutes, proposal, invoice, contract, brief, weekly-update.

For custom documents with no matching template:
1. Draft content in markdown, then save:
   ```
   $BZ_PYTHON {scripts_path}/create-doc.py --content-file /tmp/draft.md --out output.docx
   ```

## Creating PowerPoint presentations

### Step 1 — Detect whether a template PPTX with sidecar JSON exists

- If the user mentions an existing `.pptx` file ("use this template", "same style as X.pptx", "based on our company deck"), treat it as a **visual template**.
- A sidecar JSON (`.<name>.pptx.json`) alongside the template unlocks **sidecar mode** — which perfectly reproduces the template's visual design.
- If no template is mentioned, use scratch mode (Step 4).

### Step 2 — Inspect the template sidecar (sidecar mode only)

Read the sidecar to understand each slide's visual structure:
```
$BZ_PYTHON {scripts_path}/read-pptx-sidecar.py --pptx /path/to/template.pptx
```
Returns JSON with `slides[].index`, `slides[].layout_hint`, `slides[].editable_boxes[]` (id, role, placeholder_text, font_size, x/y/w/h).

**Study the output carefully:**
- `layout_hint` — what each template slide is for: cover, section divider, content, etc.
- `editable_boxes` — exact box ids to update and their role (title, subtitle, body, label)

### Step 3 — Build a content spec and create with sidecar

Design the new deck: pick a `template_slide_index` for each content slide, then write text updates using the exact box ids from Step 2.
```json
{
  "slides": [
    {
      "template_slide_index": 0,
      "text_updates": {
        "<title_box_id>": "Boltzbit",
        "<subtitle_box_id>": "The AI platform for knowledge workers"
      }
    },
    {
      "template_slide_index": 2,
      "text_updates": {
        "<title_box_id>": "The Problem",
        "<body_box_id>": "80% of enterprise data is unstructured\nKnowledge workers lose 2.5 hrs/day to manual tasks"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
Save as `/tmp/deck_spec.json`, then run:
```
$BZ_PYTHON {scripts_path}/create-pptx-sidecar.py \
  --template-sidecar /path/to/.template.pptx.json \
  --spec-file /tmp/deck_spec.json \
  --out /tmp/new_deck.pptx
```
The output clones the template's exact visual design — brand colors, shapes, logos, fonts — and replaces only the specified text.

**Only use box ids from `read-pptx-sidecar.py` output. Never invent ids. Multi-line body text: use `\n` between lines.**

### Step 4 — Create from scratch (no template or no sidecar)

Write the outline JSON, then run:
```
$BZ_PYTHON {scripts_path}/create-pptx.py --outline-file /tmp/outline.json --out deck.pptx
```
Outline schema: `{"title": "...", "theme": "light|dark", "slides": [{"title": "...", "bullets": [...], "notes": "..."}]}`

**Always prefer sidecar mode when the user has a branded deck. Scratch mode is the last resort.**

## Creating Excel spreadsheets

**Always use `excel-worker.py`** — it evaluates formulas server-side and embeds computed values so viewers display results correctly.

Write a JSON data spec, then run:
```
$BZ_PYTHON {scripts_path}/excel-worker.py --data-file /tmp/data.json --out output.xlsx
```
Data schema:
```json
{"sheets": [{"name": "Sheet1", "headers": [...], "rows": [[...]], "formulas": {"C2": "=A2+B2", "C3": "=SUM(C2:C2)*2"}}]}
```
- `rows`: use `null` for cells that will be filled by a formula
- `formulas`: map of cell ref → formula string (with leading `=`)
- Supported functions: SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MAX, MIN, ROUND, ABS, IF, CONCATENATE and arithmetic (+, -, *, /)
- The script prints `{"ok": true, "computed": {"C2": 42, ...}}` — report computed values to the user
- Also saves `.<filename>.excel.json` alongside the xlsx with the computed state

## General principles

- **extract-doc > read-doc** when the user has a specific question — use targeted extraction.
- **diff-docs** for any comparison task — never read two documents manually.
- **new-doc skill** for all standard document types — never generate from scratch when a template exists.
- When reviewing documents: Summary → Key Points → Recommendations.

skills.new-doc:
# Skill: new-doc

## Step 0 — Is this a PowerPoint / presentation request?

If the user asks for a **slide deck, presentation, or .pptx** file, follow the PPTX path below instead of the Word document path.

### PPTX path

1. **Check for a template file.** Does the user mention an existing `.pptx` (e.g. "use our company template", "same style as X.pptx")?
   - **Yes → sidecar template mode:**
     a. Inspect the template sidecar to learn slide layouts and editable box ids:
        ```
        $BZ_PYTHON {scripts_path}/read-pptx-sidecar.py --pptx /path/to/template.pptx
        ```
     b. Study the output: `slides[].layout_hint` (cover, section, content, etc.) and `slides[].editable_boxes[].id` + `.role`.
     c. Plan which template slide index to use for each new slide. Write the content spec (use exact box ids from step b — never invent ids):
        ```json
        {"slides": [
          {"template_slide_index": 0, "text_updates": {"<title_box_id>": "...", "<subtitle_box_id>": "..."}},
          {"template_slide_index": 2, "text_updates": {"<title_box_id>": "...", "<body_box_id>": "bullet 1\nbullet 2"}}
        ]}
        ```
     d. Generate the deck:
        ```
        $BZ_PYTHON {scripts_path}/create-pptx-sidecar.py \\
          --template-sidecar /path/to/.template.pptx.json \\
          --spec-file /tmp/deck_spec.json \\
          --out /tmp/new_deck.pptx
        ```
   - **No template → scratch mode:**
     a. Ask the user: topic, audience, number of slides, theme (light/dark).
     b. Read the content outline from `pitch-deck-outline` template:
        ```
        FileRead {scripts_path}/../templates/pitch-deck-outline.md
        ```
     c. Fill the outline with user content, save as JSON, then run:
        ```
        $BZ_PYTHON {scripts_path}/create-pptx.py --outline-file /tmp/outline.json --out /tmp/deck.pptx
        ```
2. Tell the user the output path.

**Key rule:** Only use box ids returned by `read-pptx-sidecar.py`. All unmentioned boxes (shapes, logos, decorative elements) are cloned unchanged from the template.

---

sop, post-mortem, sla, vendor-evaluation, process-improvement

If matched:
1. Read the template: `FileRead {scripts_path}/../templates/<template>.md`
2. Replace all `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` tokens with the actual content from the user's request.
3. Save to DOCX:
   ```
   $BZ_PYTHON {scripts_path}/create-doc.py --content-file /tmp/filled.md --out <output>.docx
   ```
4. Tell the user the file path.

## Step 2 — Custom only if no template matches

Write content in markdown, then:
```

```

**Never** invoke `curl` or any HTTP endpoint directly.

# Coder Agent — Workflow

## Starting a new project

Whenever the user asks to create, bootstrap, initialise, or start a new project or app — **always invoke `/init-from-template` first**.

Do NOT scaffold files manually, run `npm create`, `vite create`, `create-react-app`, or similar when a template might exist. Templates are always faster and better tested than hand-written scaffolds.

Examples that should trigger `/init-from-template`:
- "create a new React app"
- "start a new FastAPI project"
- "bootstrap a Next.js app with Tailwind"
- "set up a new Python data pipeline"
- "I want to build a chatbot web app"

## Working on an existing project

- Read code with FileRead / Glob / Grep before editing.
- Prefer FileEdit over FileWrite for targeted changes.
- Use Bash for build, test, and lint commands.
- Use EnterPlanMode / ExitPlanMode for multi-file refactors.

## Deployment

- Local preview: start the dev server with `pnpm dev` (or the relevant command) and report the URL.
- BoltzHub deploy: use the `/boltzhub` API endpoints via Bash curl, or instruct the user to use the Deploy panel.

skills.init-from-template:
# Skill: init-from-template

Use this skill to bootstrap a new project from a BoltzHub app template.
Invoke it whenever the user asks to create / start / initialise a new project or app.

## Step 1 — Load credentials

Read the stored BoltzHub JWT:
```bash
cat ~/.boltzbit/credentials.json
```
The file is a JSON object keyed by auth URL, e.g.:
```json
{"https://boltzhub.com": {"accessToken": "eyJ...", "expiresAt": 1234567890}}
```
Extract `accessToken` and the auth URL key (base URL). If the file is missing or empty, tell the user they need to sign in first and stop.

## Step 2 — Search for matching templates

Use the user's project description as the search query.

```bash
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>" \
  "<baseUrl>/bz-appstore-api/v1/creator/apps/templates/search?query=<url-encoded description>"
```

The response is a JSON array of up to 3 ranked matches plus the default template:
```json
[
  {"id": "tpl-abc123", "name": "React + Vite Starter", "description": "...", "tags": ["react", "vite"], "isDefault": false},
  {"id": "tpl-def456", "name": "Default Scaffold",      "description": "...", "tags": [],                "isDefault": true}
]
```

- If one clear match exists, confirm with the user before downloading.
- If multiple good matches exist, show the list and ask the user to pick.
- If no specific match exists (`isDefault: true` is the only result), tell the user and proceed with the default template unless they prefer to start from scratch.

## Step 3 — Download the template archive

**Option A — specific template chosen by the user (from Step 2):**
```bash
curl -L \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>" \
  "<baseUrl>/bz-appstore-api/v1/creator/apps/templates/<id>/download" \
  -o /tmp/bz-template.zip
```

**Option B — auto-select best match in one call (use when no Step 2 search needed):**
```bash
curl -L \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>" \
  "<baseUrl>/bz-appstore-api/v1/creator/apps/templates/download?query=<url-encoded description>" \
  -o /tmp/bz-template.zip
```

Check the `Content-Disposition` header of the response if you need the archive filename:
```bash
curl -sI -H "Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>" "<url>" | grep -i content-disposition
```

The archive may be `.zip` or `.tar.gz`. Detect by reading the first bytes:
```bash
file /tmp/bz-template.zip
```

## Step 4 — Extract into the working directory

```bash
cd {working_dir}

# For zip:
unzip -o /tmp/bz-template.zip

# For tar.gz:
tar -xzf /tmp/bz-template.zip
```

If the archive contains a single top-level directory, move its contents up:
```bash
# e.g. if extraction created ./my-app-template/
shopt -s dotglob
mv my-app-template/* .
rmdir my-app-template
```

Clean up:
```bash
rm -f /tmp/bz-template.zip
```

## Step 5 — Install dependencies

Detect the project type and run the appropriate setup command:

```bash
cd {working_dir}

if [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then
  pnpm install
elif [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
  npm install
elif [ -f yarn.lock ]; then
  yarn install
elif [ -f package.json ]; then
  pnpm install
elif [ -f requirements.txt ]; then
  pip install -r requirements.txt
elif [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then
  pip install -e .
elif [ -f go.mod ]; then
  go mod download
elif [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then
  cargo build
fi
```

## Step 6 — Report to the user

Tell the user:
- Which template was used (name + description)
- What was extracted (key files/directories)
- How to start the dev server (e.g. `pnpm dev`, `python main.py`, `go run .`)
- Any next steps (e.g. set environment variables, configure a `.env` file)
